key_insight: Syndrome records alone can be used in classical post-processing to cancel residual logical errors in quantum circuits, avoiding prior noise learning and circuit modification.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper, bias-free error mitigation for early fault-tolerant quantum computing by improving logical estimates after execution without extra quantum hardware overhead.
method: Use only measured syndrome records from logical quantum circuits.
Pair a fast in-experiment decoder with a stronger decoder in post-processing.
Apply virtual error cancellation to reduce logical bias and sampling overhead.
evidence_signal: In simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, the full-stack dual-decoder method showed sample-dependent error reduction and over three orders of magnitude suppression versus the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable regime.
watch_item: The approach relies on high-quality syndrome data and an effective post-processing decoder, so performance may be limited by decoder mismatch or experimental readout imperfections.
paper_title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
